correctness.rationale: The long-legged hypothesis ensures every same-arm pair at distance at most k occurs together in a moving window, giving exact nonzero support of the constructed real symmetric matrix. Distinct arm lengths retain a common first-k-coordinate kernel via their respective window recurrences. Summing arm-difference coefficients to zero annihilates all cross-arm and central equations, producing (m-1)k independent null vectors. A chronological endpoint-to-center and center-to-last-arm forcing sequence colors the graph using exactly (m-1)k initial black vertices. The established M<=Z inequality forces equality and the stated minimum rank. The executable reconstructs graph distances and tests actual integer witnesses and every forcing rule.

originality.rationale: The first-public 2026-10-02 graph-powers source, Proposition 9 and Conjecture 10, treats equal-leg spiders and only establishes their upper bound. Already available exact classifications for equal-length spiders and the tree-square theorem were recognized as covering those subclasses, and the new claim excludes equal lengths and k<=2. Variable independent arm lengths alter the graph and are not implied by a uniform-family theorem. The synchronized-window construction supplies a proof over every genuinely unbalanced long-legged tuple. Exact ordinary kth-power results for nonuniform long-legged spiders were not found in the inspected source full texts or targeted searches. This is a best-knowledge originality judgment, not a priority guarantee.
residual_risks: Unlocated prior theorem under other terms such as distance powers of subdivided stars or all-tree minimum-rank specializations may dominate this result.
Uniform-spider proofs might already yield the variable-length case as an unstated corollary; source and historical priorities need independent verification.

value.rationale: The 2026 initiation identifies graph-power zero forcing for spiders as an open exact-value problem; independently variable arm lengths are a canonical, highly nontrivial extension from symmetric spiders. The result determines both zero forcing and the minimum real-symmetric rank on the entire nonuniform long-legged domain at all k>=3, and the shared-prefix kernel supplies a structural explanation for complete arm-length invariance. The long-leg threshold is geometrically meaningful for the moving-window rank bound. This is substantially more than numerical tabulation or a tiny additive improvement.
